title: Why Senegal’s Pink Lake Looks Like a Dream

scenes.text: 5 km of pink water in West Africa will blow your mind
scenes.query: Lake Retba pink water aerial view

scenes.label: THE SALT THAT PAINTS THE WATER
scenes.text: Tiny algae thrive in the lake’s salty brine, turning the surface pink.
scenes.query: Lake Retba Dunaliella salina algae pink lake close-up

scenes.label: SEASONAL COLOR SHIFT
scenes.text: During the dry season the water concentrates, making the pink hue vivid; in rainy months it fades to turquoise.
scenes.query: Lake Retba seasonal color change time-lapse

scenes.label: NATURAL SALT HARVESTING
scenes.text: Local workers still collect salt by hand, a tradition that’s been alive for centuries.
scenes.query: Senegal salt harvest workers Lake Retba

scenes.text: Follow to see the world's hidden places.

description: Lake Retba’s bubble‑gum pink waters are a rare natural spectacle caused by salty algae. Dive into its colors, seasons, and centuries‑old salt harvest. Follow for more hidden natural wonders!
